verdict.rationale: Kling documents a cheaper 'std' mode alongside a pricier 'pro' mode (e.g., Motion Control at $0.126/s std vs. $0.168/s pro), which covers the cheap-draft half of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows a way to take a chosen draft and upscale it to final quality. Native 4K generation is a separate, from-scratch capability, not an upscale of an existing take. missing for 10: a documented upscale/enhance step for an existing generation, evidence that std drafts are faster, a draft-to-final workflow tying the two together, and hands-on corroboration.
